spans.text: For instance, the black population in South Carolina rose to 60% within fifty years after initial British settlement, while blacks in New York made up only about 16% of the population.

spans.text: While different varieties of African American English across the United States share regional patterns with other varieties of American English in the areas in which they are spoken, these varieties of AAE share many core patterns that make it possible to refer to a general African American English.

It is described here according to its systematic properties in the syntactic, semantic (and pragmatic), morphological and phonological components – due to its sociohistorical, sociopolitical, and sociolinguistic background related to African and creole influence and settlement patterns – that are intertwined with patterns from general American English.
